plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 11: Angular Momentum
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single three-dimensional diagram of a spinning top together with the vectors that govern its precession. A coordinate frame is drawn with z vertical, y to the right, and x angled toward the lower left, meeting at the origin O where the point of the top rests. The top is a rounded, banded body in blue and orange capped by a short cylindrical stem, its symmetry axis tilted away from z by the angle theta. A heavy black arrow labeled r runs from O to the center of mass, marked with an X and labeled 'CM', where a red arrow labeled 'M g' points straight down. From that same point an orange arrow labeled tau extends outward and slightly upward, with a curved leader to the expression 'tau = r x M g'. A green loop labeled omega circles the stem to give the spin sense, and a long orange arrow labeled L lies along the tilted axis, reaching a dashed horizontal circle drawn above the top. On that circle a radial orange arrow labeled 'L sin theta' and a tangential arrow labeled 'dL = tau dt' meet at a small angle marked 'd phi', while a curved black arrow labeled omega sub p at the upper left gives the direction of precession. Placing the torque perpendicular to L lets the reader see that the tip of L sweeps around the circle instead of tipping over. The construction sets up the calculation of how fast a gravitationally torqued top precesses about the vertical.

elements: coordinate frame: z-axis vertical, y-axis to the right, x-axis angled toward lower left, meeting at origin O
spinning top body: rounded blue bulbous form with an orange band, cinched waist below, pointed tip resting at O
short cylindrical stem on top of the body along the tilted symmetry axis
angle theta arc between the z-axis and the top's symmetry axis at O
black arrow r from O to the center of mass, CM marked with a small X
red downward arrow Mg from CM
orange arrow tau from CM, horizontal-ish outward, with curved leader to label 'tau = r x Mg'
green circular loop around the stem labeled omega (spin sense)
long orange arrow L along the tilted symmetry axis from near CM up to the dashed circle
dashed horizontal circle centered on the z-axis at the height of L's tip
orange radial arrow from the z-axis to L's tip labeled 'L sin theta'
short tangential orange arrow at L's tip labeled 'dL = tau dt'
small angle wedge labeled d phi at the center of the dashed circle between successive radial positions
curved black arrow labeled omega_p at upper left showing precession direction

interactions.label: Play precession
interactions.teaches: As the top precesses, the tip of L sweeps the dashed circle while |L| stays constant — torque changes the direction of angular momentum, not its magnitude, since dL is always tangential (perpendicular to L)

interactions.label: Tilt angle θ
interactions.teaches: The lean of the top sets the L sin θ radius of the precession circle and rescales the dφ construction, connecting the geometry of the tilted angular momentum to the precession step

interactions.label: Torque |τ|
interactions.teaches: Larger torque lengthens the dL arrow (and hence the precession rate ωp = τ/(L sin θ)) while L keeps its length — torque redirects angular momentum rather than growing it

demo_steps.title: Torque on the tilted top
demo_steps.narration: With the top at rest in the diagram, gravity Mg acts down at CM, and τ = r × Mg points tangentially. Notice τ is perpendicular to L — that is why L can only change direction.

demo_steps.title: Watch L precess
demo_steps.narration: Play the precession: the tip of the L arrow sweeps around the dashed circle with constant length, each step of dL pointing along the tangent, advancing L through angle dφ.

demo_steps.title: Increase the tilt
demo_steps.narration: Raising θ to 50° widens the L sin θ circle. Since ωp = τ/(L sin θ), the top precesses more slowly on a larger circle.

demo_steps.title: Stronger torque
demo_steps.narration: Increasing |τ| lengthens the dL arrow — each precession step is bigger, so ωp increases, but the length of L still never changes.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: origin O at (0,0,0); z-axis up ~5 units, y-axis ~4 to the right, x-axis ~3 toward lower left (standard physics triad). Top body: a lathe/teardrop profile ~2.2 units tall from tip at O to cap, max radius ~1.1, blue (#a8cce0) with an orange (#f0b44c) band around its widest third; stem is a cylinder radius 0.25, height 0.9 continuing along the tilted axis. The whole top (body + stem) is rotated about O by θ from the z-axis, tilted toward +y/-x quadrant as in the source (top leans right). CM sits on the symmetry axis ~1.5 units from O (inside the upper body), marked with a small X. Vectors: r — thick black arrow O→CM; Mg — red (#cc2222) arrow straight down from CM, length ~1; τ — orange (#e8862a) arrow from CM pointing perpendicular to both r and g (roughly toward viewer/right), length scaled by torque slider (0.6–1.8). L — long orange arrow along the symmetry axis from near CM, fixed length ~3.2 regardless of sliders, tip reaching the dashed circle. Dashed circle: radius L sin θ, centered on z-axis at height |L|cos θ above CM height, dashed dark grey line; 'L sin θ' radial arrow drawn inside it in orange; dL — short tangential orange arrow at L's tip, length proportional to torque slider; dφ wedge between current and next radial line; curved ωp arrow at upper-left rim of circle; green (#5a9a3c) spin loop around stem labeled ω. Key physics: ωp = τ/(L sin θ) must drive the animation speed; |L| invariant.
interactionPlan.notes: Rotate the entire top assembly (body, stem, r, CM, Mg, τ, L) about the z-axis during the precession animation, keeping the Mg arrow always vertical (it rotates position, not direction) — simplest is to rotate the assembly and counter-rotate Mg's direction. Rebuild the dashed circle, L sin θ radial arrow, and dφ wedge reactively on θ change. dL arrow length and animation angular speed both scale with the torque slider. Use arrowheads (ConeGeometry) for all vectors; dashed circle via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances. Keep Mg red and L/τ in the same orange family as the source, with text sprites for labels r, Mg, τ, L, ω, ωp, θ, dφ, L sin θ, dL = τdt, CM, O.

authoredContext:
The figure shows the forces acting on a spinning top. The torque produced is perpendicular to the angular momentum vector. This changes the direction of the angular momentum vector L→ according to dL→=τ→dt, but not its magnitude. The top precesses around a vertical axis, since the torque is always horizontal and perpendicular to L→. If the top is not spinning, it acquires angular momentum in the direction of the torque, and it rotates around a horizontal axis, falling over just as we would expect.

We can calculate the precession rate of the top in the figure. From the figure, we see that the magnitude of the torque is

The force of gravity acting on the center of mass produces a torque τ→ in the direction perpendicular to L→. The magnitude of L→ doesn’t change but its direction does, and the top precesses about the z-axis.

An x y z coordinate system is show, with x out of the page, y to the right, and z up. The origin is point O. A top is shown with its point at the origin and its axis tilted by an angle theta away from the vertical z axis, clockwise as we view it. The vector r extends from the origin to the center of the mass, labeled as C M, of the top. The force M g acts downward at the center of mass. The torque, tau, about the origin is equal to vector r crossed with M vector g. This torque is a vector in the x y plane, perpendicular to the r vector, into the page. The angular velocity, omega, of the top is counterclockwise as viewed from above. The angular momentum, L, is in the same direction as the r vector, tilted up along the axis of the top. The circle traced by the precession of the top is shown as a horizontal circle above the top. The precession angular velocity omega sub p is counterclockwise as viewed from above. The radius of the precession circle is L sine theta. The vector d L is tangent to the circle, pointing into the page, and is equal to vector tau d t. The triangle formed L sine theta and d L is shown, and the angle across from d L is labeled as d phi.

We can experience this phenomenon first hand by holding a spinning bicycle wheel and trying to rotate it about an axis perpendicular to the spin axis. As shown in the figure, the person applies forces perpendicular to the spin axis in an attempt to rotate the wheel, but instead, the wheel axis starts to change direction to her left due to the applied torque.

interactions.label: Play precession
interactions.teaches: As the top precesses, the tip of L sweeps the dashed circle while |L| stays constant — torque changes the direction of angular momentum, not its magnitude, since dL is always tangential (perpendicular to L)

interactions.label: Tilt angle θ
interactions.teaches: The lean of the top sets the L sin θ radius of the precession circle and rescales the dφ construction, connecting the geometry of the tilted angular momentum to the precession step

interactions.label: Torque |τ|
interactions.teaches: Larger torque lengthens the dL arrow (and hence the precession rate ωp = τ/(L sin θ)) while L keeps its length — torque redirects angular momentum rather than growing it

demo_steps.title: Torque on the tilted top
demo_steps.narration: With the top at rest in the diagram, gravity Mg acts down at CM, and τ = r × Mg points tangentially. Notice τ is perpendicular to L — that is why L can only change direction.

demo_steps.title: Watch L precess
demo_steps.narration: Play the precession: the tip of the L arrow sweeps around the dashed circle with constant length, each step of dL pointing along the tangent, advancing L through angle dφ.

demo_steps.title: Increase the tilt
demo_steps.narration: Raising θ to 50° widens the L sin θ circle. Since ωp = τ/(L sin θ), the top precesses more slowly on a larger circle.

demo_steps.title: Stronger torque
demo_steps.narration: Increasing |τ| lengthens the dL arrow — each precession step is bigger, so ωp increases, but the length of L still never changes.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: origin O at (0,0,0); z-axis up ~5 units, y-axis ~4 to the right, x-axis ~3 toward lower left (standard physics triad). Top body: a lathe/teardrop profile ~2.2 units tall from tip at O to cap, max radius ~1.1, blue (#a8cce0) with an orange (#f0b44c) band around its widest third; stem is a cylinder radius 0.25, height 0.9 continuing along the tilted axis. The whole top (body + stem) is rotated about O by θ from the z-axis, tilted toward +y/-x quadrant as in the source (top leans right). CM sits on the symmetry axis ~1.5 units from O (inside the upper body), marked with a small X. Vectors: r — thick black arrow O→CM; Mg — red (#cc2222) arrow straight down from CM, length ~1; τ — orange (#e8862a) arrow from CM pointing perpendicular to both r and g (roughly toward viewer/right), length scaled by torque slider (0.6–1.8). L — long orange arrow along the symmetry axis from near CM, fixed length ~3.2 regardless of sliders, tip reaching the dashed circle. Dashed circle: radius L sin θ, centered on z-axis at height |L|cos θ above CM height, dashed dark grey line; 'L sin θ' radial arrow drawn inside it in orange; dL — short tangential orange arrow at L's tip, length proportional to torque slider; dφ wedge between current and next radial line; curved ωp arrow at upper-left rim of circle; green (#5a9a3c) spin loop around stem labeled ω. Key physics: ωp = τ/(L sin θ) must drive the animation speed; |L| invariant.
interactionPlan.notes: Rotate the entire top assembly (body, stem, r, CM, Mg, τ, L) about the z-axis during the precession animation, keeping the Mg arrow always vertical (it rotates position, not direction) — simplest is to rotate the assembly and counter-rotate Mg's direction. Rebuild the dashed circle, L sin θ radial arrow, and dφ wedge reactively on θ change. dL arrow length and animation angular speed both scale with the torque slider. Use arrowheads (ConeGeometry) for all vectors; dashed circle via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances. Keep Mg red and L/τ in the same orange family as the source, with text sprites for labels r, Mg, τ, L, ω, ωp, θ, dφ, L sin θ, dL = τdt, CM, O.
